decisions.reason: The abstract of Lechuga et al. (2015) explicitly retests 'Karpicke and Blunt (2011)', which showed in college students that retrieval practice produced more learning from educational texts than concept mapping (thought to involve elaborative processing) on a 1-week delayed test, and deposited reference bib16 (chunk 5) plus the recovered Science paper and supplement (10.1126/science.1199327, Karpicke & Blunt, 2011) confirm that exact finding (elaborative concept mapping with texts present vs. free-recall retrieval practice, including a null prior-experience check in Exp. 1 SOM). However, shipped row 588 is Blunt & Karpicke (2011), 'Concept Mapping as a Retrieval Practice Activity' (10.1037/e520602012-521, a 2011 Psychonomic Society poster / PsycEXTRA dataset record). While recovered Blunt & Karpicke (2014, 10.1037/a0035934) tests retrieval-based concept mapping in the absence of texts as a conceptual replication of Science 2011 (making it a plausible journal counterpart to the 2011 poster title), the 2011 poster's actual content could not be recovered (HTTP 403/empty archive) and Lechuga et al.'s full text is unavailable. Because reversed author order and different title/DOI alone cannot prove whether 10.1037/e520602012-521 is an alternate report of the Science 2011 study or a distinct study, original binding for row 588 (and dependent missing_row target 0) is undeterminable.

decisions.quote:
Further evidence that concept mapping is not better than repeated retrieval as a tool for learning from texts
M. Teresa Lechuga; Juana M. Ortega-Tudela; Carlos J. Gómez-Ariza
Abstract
Karpicke and Blunt (2011) showed in college students that retrieval practice produced more learning from educational texts than concept mapping on a 1-week delayed test. This finding is surprising since concept mapping is thought to involve elaborative processing. Hence, the present study (N = 84; 76 females) aimed to examine whether the advantage of repeated retrieval remains when concept mapping is performed by ad hoc trained students or students who regularly utilise concept maps to prepare for exams. While the results essentially replicate Karpicke and Blunt's finding which shows that retrieval practice leads to better overall performance than concept mapping, this effect was less pronounced for people with experience using this technique than it was for trained participants. However, the current source remains abstract-only (with Methods and Results unavailable), and the requested outcome field is bound to shipped row 588 (Blunt & Karpicke, 2011, 'Concept Mapping as a Retrieval Practice Activity', 10.1037/e520602012-521). Because the 2011 PsycEXTRA poster/dataset content is unrecovered and it cannot be established from primary evidence whether 10.1037/e520602012-521 is an alternate report of the retested 2011 Science elaborative-concept-mapping finding or a distinct retrieval-based concept-mapping study (as in Blunt & Karpicke, 2014, 10.1037/a0035934) not retested here, the original-specific outcome for shipped row 588 is undeterminable.
